# host-baselines.tsv — the per-host reference artifacts gate-p5 judges against.
# Tab-separated, tracked, human-diffable, and keyed on THE EXACT CPU-MODEL STRING
# gate-p5's README criterion greps (`remote_probe | cut -d'|' -f1`). One key shared
# with the criterion that consumes it, so the registry can never disagree with the
# check about who a host is.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A criterion whose reference artifact predates the host's
# admission cannot judge that host: the bar-derivation set, the README row and the
# archived baseline are all artifacts of runs a newly admitted host was not in, and
# convicting it for its absence from them measures its admission date rather than
# its code. That is the BASELINE-REGISTERED class (ruled 2026-08-21, #6), and this
# file is what a host graduates INTO.
# THE GATE PROPOSES ROWS AND NEVER WRITES THIS FILE. An instrument minting the
# reference it will judge against is self-certification, so gate-p5 emits a fully
# formed candidate row to build/baseline-candidates-<rev>-<run>.tsv and stops there;
# landing it is a reviewed commit act, exactly like every reference artifact before
# it. The three states it decides between come from the archive, not from a flag:
#   registered   — a row here for this era → judged at (baseline - BASELINE_MARGIN),
#                  derivation printed
#   new          — no row, and no witness row for (this cpu_model, this era)
#                  → BASELINE: verdict green-compatible, both candidate rows emitted
#   owing        — no row, but a witness row exists → FAIL, naming the unmet registration
# BASELINE IS SINGLE-SHOT PER HOST PER ERA, and the thing that spends it is a TRACKED
# witness row in scripts/judged-runs.tsv, keyed (cpu_model, era). It is not the run's own
# archive: build/ is gitignored, so an archive-derived witness is right on the operator's
# machine and wrong on every other one (#114). What the tracked form costs is stated
# where it is weaker than it sounds — see judged-runs.tsv and `baseline_spent`.
# EVERY ROW IS SCOPED TO AN ERA (column 3, scripts/measurement-eras.tsv), because a
# baseline is a number an instrument produced and a changed instrument changes it for
# reasons that are not the host's code. Judging a pinned reading against a baseline
# minted from free-placement draws would book THE METHODOLOGY DELTA AS HOST DRIFT — the
# cross-denominator sin this registry exists to prevent, arriving through the registry.
# So a row from another era does not match, an instrument change renders BASELINE
# fleet-wide once, and an era cannot be conjured by operator convenience: it takes a
# dated §5/§7 amendment plus a both-arms transition archive (ruled 2026-08-21, #6).
# BASELINES ARE IMMUTABLE except by the two doors that already exist in law:
# supersession by a tighter re-measure, or dated re-registration citing a named code
# change. Either way the row's estimator, source and grounds move with the value;
# provenance is the row, not a footnote.
# NOT IN HERE, on purpose: the CPU models that DERIVED THE BAR A ROW WOULD BE FOR. Their
# reference artifact does not predate their admission — they are the artifact — so they stay
# on the fleet bar, and gate-p5 FAILS a host claimed by both a derivation list and this
# registry rather than picking a winner. Per-host convergence for them is a post-tag option,
# not something smuggled in with this mechanism.
# THERE WAS A SECOND LIST AND IT IS RETIRED (#119 then #177). From 2026-08-30 `scale/Strsm`
# rows were excluded for SCALE_DERIVED_FROM's THREE models — one more than CEIL_DERIVED_FROM's
# two, including the Intel 8124M that has three `share/*` rows below — so the same host was
# legitimately registry-governed on one criterion and fleet-governed on the other, and adding a
# `scale/Strsm` row "for consistency" would have convicted it of a conflict on a bar it helped
# derive. The T8/T1 criterion is retired as of 2026-10-05; there is ONE derivation list again
# and the hazard is gone rather than guarded. The `scale/Strsm` rows below stay as what they
# are: closed-era rows no criterion in this tree reads.
# EVERY JUDGED CRITERION IS KEYED `<criterion>/<tile>/<backend>/<row>` from era `ceil8`
# (#177, 2026-10-05; #167 did it for `peak/*` on 2026-10-01 and said why). A baseline is a
# claim about what a KERNEL achieved on a host, so a key with no kernel in it carries that
# claim across a dispatch change: the EIGHT arm64 rows below — six `share/*` and two
# `scale/Strsm` — were measured on `8x8/neon`, read off `029e24f`'s own `keel-bench-kern` marker
# in the archives their source column names, and were being applied to `3x24/neon` two
# promotions later. The three amd64 rows are `2x32/avx512` from `969c360` and have not moved;
# a shape-blind key cannot tell those two cases apart, which is why the key and not a one-off
# correction is the fix. The bare keys are therefore NOT a
# second spelling still in service — they are the old era's, and the era column is what keeps
# them out of a current lookup. A re-key WITHOUT an era boundary was attempted on 2026-10-05
# and correctly refused: the witness in judged-runs.tsv is keyed (cpu_model, era) and not on
# the criterion, so a re-key alone makes this registry miss while the witness stands and every
# row resolves `owing`. The era boundary is the door.
# THE FIRST ROWS LANDED 2026-08-28, and what unblocked them is worth recording, because
# both of the reasons this file was empty had to be discharged and only one of them was
# about waiting. The first: keel-skx's share baseline cannot be imported from the
# free-instrument runs that measured it (5ec5fea, 33de3b2), because a published reference
# is an estimator, never a draw (§5 rule 16), and both of those are single draws. That is
# now satisfied by a median over the era's TWO judged archives. The second, and it is why
# the file was empty for the WHOLE FLEET rather than for one host: no row can exist in an
# era before the run that measures it, so every host rendered BASELINE on the transition
# run, by design and once. Era `pinned8` now has both arms preserved and is closed.
# THE VALUES ARE NOT THE PRINTED SHARES, and this is the non-obvious part of the
# derivation. A share is net of BOTH intervals (bench_ratio_lo: the rate's low bound over
# the ceiling's high bound), so it is a function of the CI instrument — and #116, which
# fixed a mirrored one-sided median CI, landed at b13f398, BETWEEN the era's two judged
# revs. Take four (6ba6566) therefore PRINTED shares computed with the over-wide pre-#116
# bounds, and pooling those printed numbers with 969c360's would have averaged across an
# instrument change: the cross-denominator error this file's era column exists to prevent,
# arriving through the pool instead of through the era. So take four is recomputed from its
# archived raw samples under the current instrument, exactly as CEIL_FRACTION was
# (969c360's commit message; §5 rule 16). Positive control: the same recomputation
# reproduces 969c360's printed 31.2/31.5/30.6 to the digit. The correction moves every
# affected row UP — 29.7→30.4 and 29.8→30.1, Ssyrk unchanged — which is the direction an
# over-wide interval predicts, and it matters because pooling the printed values would have
# registered baselines 0.35 and 0.15 points LOW on two of three criteria, i.e. a
# permanently looser bar with nothing to reopen it (§5 rule 15: the flattering direction is
# the half nobody re-examines).
# NO ROW FOR keel-zen4 OR keel-zen5, deliberately and not by omission: both are in
# CEIL_DERIVED_FROM, and gate-p5 FAILS a host claimed by both that list and this registry
# rather than picking a winner. They are the artifact, so they stay on the fleet bar.
# columns, tab-separated:
#   1 cpu_model  the exact string the host reports, as gate-p5 greps it
#   2 criterion  what the baseline is a baseline FOR (e.g. share/Sgemm, scale/Strsm)
#   3 era        the instrument that produced it (scripts/measurement-eras.tsv)
#   4 baseline   the reference value; the bar is this less BASELINE_MARGIN
#   5 estimator  how it was reduced from samples, with N and the runs named
#   6 source     the archived log the value is recomputable from
#   7 as_of      the date the row was landed
#   8 grounds    why this host has its own baseline rather than the fleet's
cpu_model
column5: estimator
column8: grounds
